title: These 2 Tech Stocks Both Fell 29% on Friday. Are They Buying Opportunities Now?
detail:
These 2 Tech Stocks Both Fell 29% on Friday. Are They Buying Opportunities Now?
Matt Frankel, CFP®, The Motley Fool
Mon, November 2, 2026 at 12:24 PM MST 5 min read
INTC
RDDT
^IXIC
NVDA

Trading disclosure

Friday was a rough day for tech stocks in general. The Nasdaq Composite fell by nearly 3%. But two stocks in particular had days that will go down in history after issuing their latest earnings reports.

Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) fell by nearly 29% on Friday, erasing roughly $140 billion in market value. It was the chipmaker's worst day since July 1974. Reddit (NYSE:RDDT) also fell by about 29% after its earnings report, its worst day since it went public in 2024.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

To be clear, neither company had a bad quarter. Intel beat its own forecast, and Reddit grew its revenue by more than half. Here's what went wrong for each, and why the two problems are more connected than they might seem.

Intel had a good quarter and a bad forecast

Intel's third-quarter revenue grew 21% year over year to $16.5 billion, and adjusted earnings per share of $0.52 came in well above the company's own guidance. Its data center and AI segment was the standout, with revenue up 78% to $7.3 billion. CFO David Zinsner called it the company's strongest data center growth in 15 years.

The problem was the outlook. Intel expects fourth-quarter revenue of $15 billion to $16 billion, well below the roughly $17 billion analysts expected. Management also expects adjusted EPS of just $0.25, while analysts were looking for about $0.43. Intel's adjusted gross margin is expected to fall to about 38% from 44.1% in the third quarter.

The biggest culprit is the PC market. AI data centers are absorbing so many memory chips that laptop and desktop prices are rising, and Intel now expects PC shipments to fall about 12% this year and another 10% in 2027. An accident at its factory in Israel will also cost roughly $300 million of fourth-quarter revenue.

It's also worth noting how much optimism was already priced in. Intel's stock nearly quadrupled from the start of the year to its June high, and even after Friday it's still up more than 70% in 2026.

Reddit grew fast, but its traffic is slipping

Reddit's third-quarter revenue rose 53% to $895 million, ahead of analysts' estimates, and adjusted EBITDA jumped 70% to $402 million. By most measures, it was an excellent quarter.

However, management said search engine traffic fell meaningfully, and the decline accelerated as the quarter went on. According to CEO Steve Huffman, search referrals fell by more than 1 million per week on average in October, and Google's AI Mode "does not drive traffic." U.S. daily users slipped 2% to 50.7 million, and Reddit warned that total daily users could fall by a low-double-digit percentage this quarter. Its profit guidance also came in a bit below analysts' estimates.

5 must-read analyst questions from Reddit's Q3 earnings call

Reddit's third quarter results prompted a significant negative market reaction, despite year-on-year revenue growth and margin expansion. Management attributed the quarter's performance to robust advertising demand, with strong gains in both pricing and impressions, but also acknowledged that a sharp decline in search referral traffic—especially from Google—pressured user growth. CEO Steve Huffman highlighted that logged-in and app user engagement remained the primary revenue driver, stating, "We grew logged in and app dial sequentially. Together, these make up the vast majority of engagement and over 80% of the monetization on Reddit."

Is now the time to buy RDDT? Find out in our full research report (it's free).

Reddit (RDDT) Q3 2026 highlights:

Revenue $895 million vs S&P analysts' estimates of $877.2 million (53% year-on-year growth, 2% beat)

Adjusted EPS $2.07 vs S&P analysts' estimates of $1.95 (6.1% beat)

Adjusted EBITDA $402.3 million vs analyst estimates of $397.1 million (44.9% margin, 1.3% beat)

Revenue guidance $1.02 billion at the midpoint for Q4 2026, below analyst estimates of $1.04 billion

EBITDA guidance $495 million at the midpoint for Q4 2026, below analyst estimates of $509.4 million

Operating margin 29.2%, up from 23.7% in the same quarter last year

Domestic daily active visitors 50.7 million, down 900,000 year on year

Market capitalization $17.65 billion

While we enjoy listening to the management's commentary, our favorite part of earnings calls is the analyst questions. Those are unscripted and can often highlight topics that management teams would rather avoid or topics where the answer is complicated. Here is what has caught our attention.

Our top 5 analyst questions from Reddit's Q3 earnings call

Benjamin Black (Deutsche Bank) asked about the rationale and expected impact of moving to a logged-in only experience. CEO Steve Huffman clarified that this transition aims to improve engagement and ad targeting but acknowledged trade-offs in reach, while COO Jen Wong highlighted that over 80% of monetization already comes from this user base.

Josh Beck (Raymond James) inquired about the drivers behind the decline in Google traffic and the scaling potential of paid user marketing. Huffman attributed traffic drops primarily to AI-driven search changes, while Wong said early app install campaigns show promising retention rates but are still small in scale.

John Colantuoni (Jefferies) questioned the extent and permanence of the logged-in only shift and engagement trends. Huffman said the transition is a test but will be permanent, with engagement improvements among app users partially offsetting overall traffic declines.

Tom Champion (Piper) asked if the current strategic environment resembles past inflection points and about future ARPU growth. Huffman referenced past periods of change and said product improvements will help drive daily habits, while Vollero pointed to the unique commercial potential of Reddit's user base for further ARPU gains.

Jason Helfstein (Oppenheimer) sought clarity on how to model user monetization after the shift and whether the platform will become less accessible to web scrapers. Huffman responded that testing will inform boundaries and confirmed that the move will make Reddit harder to scrape, protecting valuable data.

title: Reddit (RDDT) Stock Fair Value Moves Lower After Analysts Cut Targets On User Concerns
detail:
Reddit (RDDT) Stock Fair Value Moves Lower After Analysts Cut Targets On User Concerns
Bailey Pemberton
Mon, November 2, 2026 at 9:08 AM MST 4 min read
RDDT
Trade Reddit on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

The modelled fair value price target for Reddit has been cut from US$216.35 to US$167.85, a sizeable reset that puts a lower ceiling on what analysts see as reasonable upside for the stock. This shift lines up with recent Street commentary, where firms are reacting to softer user trends, changing search traffic patterns, and a different valuation framework, even as they still point to healthy advertising demand. As you read on, you will see how this updated price target fits into the broader Reddit story and what to watch as the narrative evolves.

Analyst Price Targets don't always capture the full story. Head over to our Company Report to find new ways to value Reddit.

What Wall Street Has Been Saying

Recent commentary on Reddit clusters around a clear trade off. Analysts are marking down valuation targets as they factor in weaker user trends and Google search referral pressure. At the same time, many still point to solid advertising demand and monetization progress, which keeps a mix of Buy, Neutral, and downgraded ratings across the Street.

🐂 Bullish Takeaways

Firms including Citi, Guggenheim, Truist, B. Riley, Morgan Stanley, Raymond James and DA Davidson still see enough business execution on revenue and advertising to justify Buy or stronger ratings on Reddit even after cutting price targets.

Several research houses such as Goldman Sachs and Citi highlight healthy advertising momentum and monetization, with pressure described as concentrated in lower value logged out traffic rather than Reddit's logged in and app users.

Deutsche Bank and Evercore ISI ad channel checks flag Reddit alongside Meta and Google as relatively well positioned in advertising budgets, with Reddit finishing ahead of plan in some recent checks.

🐻 Bearish Takeaways

Evercore ISI, DA Davidson and others point to U.S. and global daily active user pressure tied to Google referrals, which now feeds into sharply lower price targets, in some cases more than halving prior Reddit valuations.

KeyBanc, Oppenheimer, Wells Fargo, Citizens and BofA flag risks around the shift to a logged in only experience, potential volatility from AI search changes at Google and uncertainty around user durability that may cap valuation multiples for Reddit.

title: Reddit Stock Crashes Again. Is the Stock a Buy on the Dip or a Value Trap?
detail:
Reddit Stock Crashes Again. Is the Stock a Buy on the Dip or a Value Trap?
Geoffrey Seiler, The Motley Fool
Mon, November 2, 2026 at 7:48 AM MST 5 min read
RDDT
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

For the second straight quarter, shares of Reddit (NYSE: RDDT) got absolutely pummeled following its earnings report. The stock fell 21% in the session after its Q2 report, while it plunged 29% after releasing its Q3 results.

While the social media company continues to see rapid revenue growth and the stock is cheap, it's increasingly looking like a potential value trap.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Soaring revenue, but problems loom

Reddit has been seeing rapid revenue growth, and that continued in Q3, with revenue surging 53% year over year to $895 million. That handily topped the $878 million analyst consensus, as compiled by LSEG.

Ad revenue jumped 54% to $847 million, with other revenue, which includes data licensing, rose 35% to $48 million. U.S ad revenue climbed 51%, while international ad revenue jumped 68%. Growth was led by lower funnel performance revenue, like shopping apps and app installations, while upper funnel video revenue more than doubled.

The company continued to add new users to its platform, but the pace is slowing. Daily users increased 12% to 130.3 million, while weekly users grew by 16% to 515.2 million. However, the daily user number fell short of analyst expectations of 133.7 million users. Meanwhile, more valuable U.S. daily users fell 2% to 50.7 million and missed the 53.5 million analyst consensus.

User growth is one of the big reasons for the collapse in Reddit's stock price and Alphabet's Google search engine is one of the big reasons behind this. CEO Steve Huffman said Alphabet has "shifted in their relationship with the rest of the Internet," as AI Overviews and AI Mode push links down the search page and are driving less traffic to websites. He also believes that Reddit's "machine-translated" content is also being ranked lower." Reddit uses machine learning to translate posts into other languages.

Given this shift, Reddit saw an average decline of 1 million referrals per week in October. It said that if the trend continues, daily active users could drop by low double digits in Q4. In response, the company plans to require all users to create accounts to access its platform moving forward. Currently, around 80% of its revenue comes from logged-in users.

While traffic is becoming an issue, the company has been doing a nice job of monetizing its current user base. Global average revenue per user (ARPU) climbed 36% to $6.87, while U.S. ARPU surged 53% to $13.82. Reddit has been investing in machine learning and automated ad tools that are improving advertising campaigns and boosting ad performance.

Oracle upgraded, Reddit downgraded: Wall Street's top analyst calls

The most talked about and market moving research calls around Wall Street are now in one place. Here are today's research calls that investors need to know, as compiled by The Fly.

Top 5 Upgrades:

Stephens upgraded Oracle (ORCL) to Overweight from Equal Weight with a price target of $213, up from $185. The firm says the company's investor day resolved its biggest questions, with Oracle pointing to lower cloud infrastructure funding and higher free cash flow.

Phillip Securities upgraded Amazon.com (AMZN) to Buy from Accumulate with a price target of $330, up from $320, following the Q3 report. The firm says Amazon's "strong" demand visibility supports its "aggressive" capital expenditures.

Deutsche Bank upgraded CrowdStrike (CRWD) to Buy from Hold with a price target of $300, up from $240. The market has still not appreciated the extent to which AI will expand the market for cybersecurity, the firm tells investors in a research note.

Evercore ISI upgraded Clorox (CLX) to In Line from Underperform with a $99 price target ahead of the company reporting after the close. The firm, whose estimates are largely at consensus, believes Clorox shares appropriately discount the risk of an earnings reset, while adding that the appointment of Fabian Garcia as CEO brings "proven turnaround experience."

Northland upgraded both Applied Optoelectronics (AAOI) and Coherent (COHR) to Outperform and maintain the firm's respective price targets of $120 and $280. Along with steep pullbacks in the shares, the firm says Marvell Technology's (MRVL) agreement to acquire Lumentum (LITE) highlights the value of scarce Photonic device capability for large AI chip suppliers alongside compute and networking ICs.

Top 5 Downgrades:

Evercore ISI downgraded Reddit (RDDT) to In Line from Outperform with a price target of $120, down from $265, and has also removed its tactical outperform call on Reddit. The company reported "beat-and-lower" Q3 results, the firm notes, adding that it is "incrementally more concerned" about Reddit's user durability, with U.S. daily active users dropping 2% year-over-year and the company warning that global daily active users could fall by a low-double-digit percentage in Q4 from 130M if search referral losses continue at October's pace.

Morgan Stanley downgraded Coinbase (COIN) to Underweight from Equal Weight with a price target of $120, down from $258. The firm says confidence in Coinbase's earnings recovery has deteriorated.

Truist downgraded Alnylam (ALNY) to Hold from Buy with a price target of $225, down from $315. Following the Q3 report, the outlook for Amvuttra "has become meaningfully less certain," the firm tells investors in a research note.

Goldman Sachs downgraded Floor & Decor (FND) to Sell from Neutral with a price target of $38, down from $53, following the Q3 report. The firm cites the company's decelerating quarter-to-date comps, macro-driven sales headwinds, and Q4 gross margin pressures from escalating supply chain costs for the downgrade.

Morgan Stanley downgraded Camtek (CAMT) to Underweight from Equal Weight with a price target of $126, down from $152. The company can approach its mid-term financial model by 2029, but much of this upside is already priced into the shares, the firm says.
